captain_obvious_correction.refined_question: WHAT INFORMATION ABOUT A SOURCE SURVIVES THE OCEANIC CHANNEL WELL ENOUGH FOR A RECEIVER TO RECONSTRUCT ITS IDENTITY?
captain_obvious_correction.reason: The January question asked who reads. BA16 adds the prior question of identifiability: whether the forward map preserved enough source provenance for any reader to invert it.

receive_direction.meaning: External acoustic, mechanical, thermal, chemical or radiative forcing can alter physical ocean state.
receive_direction.boundary: This is physical reception/state transition, not semantic understanding.

send_direction.meaning: Ocean-internal sources and states can propagate signals that are measurable elsewhere.

ocean_transceiver_model.bidirectional_infrastructure_example: OOI Regional Cabled Array provides real-time two-way communication between shore and seafloor/water-column instruments.

supports: field-derived time-varying underwater acoustic impulse responses

external_reality_controls.supports: ocean measurements -> float -> satellite -> shore receiving stations -> data centres; separates medium/object from receiver and storage roles
engineered real-time two-way communication to ocean sensors/instruments and shore
hydrophone as physical transducer converting underwater pressure variations into electrical signals
subsea fiber can be used as distributed acoustic sensing infrastructure across large ocean/earth regions
external_reality_controls.date_note: experiment ran Nov 2025 through Jan 2026; retained only as external engineering context, not evidence for January JANUS foresight

ba16_inverse_problem_bridge.interpretation: A downstream reader cannot recover source identity that the forward map destroyed, even with zero measurement noise and perfect computation.
ba16_inverse_problem_bridge.boundary: Scoped inverse-problem analogy plus exact toy quotient theorem; not a theorem about all ocean processes.

packet_42_gate.ba16_toy_quotient: erase j by replacing middle two bits with 00
packet_42_gate.exact_result: All four sources share the same quotient codeword 100010 after j is erased; a perfect reader can recover the class but not which member was the source.
packet_42_gate.scientific_role: negative-control packet for identifiability; not a hidden-message claim

janus_spiral.ORIGIN: January Ocean Server / WHO IS THE READER?
janus_spiral.FORWARD: Represent sea as a physical state-bearing channel/substrate capable of both receiving forcing and sending observable signals.
janus_spiral.REVERSE: Ask whether source identity can be reconstructed from readback.
janus_spiral.HRAIN: Separate channel observability from source identifiability.
janus_spiral.INAIHR: Connect BA16 many-to-one quotient and Hitchhiker answer-without-question only as discovery analogies.
janus_spiral.INFORMATION_GAIN: Reader capability is bounded by information preserved by the forward map and by correctness of channel calibration.
janus_spiral.PREDICTION: More independent receiver views can improve recovery of preserved information but cannot restore provenance bits erased before observation.
janus_spiral.DEMIHEAD: Reject ocean=literal server, receiver=consciousness, 42=message, and any inference from date/time coincidence.
janus_spiral.RETURN: Replace WHO READS? with WHAT SURVIVES, HOW IS IT TRANSDUCED, AND IS THE SOURCE IDENTIFIABLE?
janus_spiral.ORIGIN_PRIME: Can a preregistered receiver recover source identity across raw measured underwater channels, and does failure decompose into noise, channel mismatch, or irreversible quotient loss?

next_gates.plan: Run the frozen 64-packet and quotient protocol through actual Zenodo field-derived impulse-response/noise MAT files from the UWA Channel Library.

Use public ocean-observatory time series to test external forcing -> ocean state -> later readback with frozen lags and held-out prediction; claim ceiling is predictive physical response, never agency.
Use hydrophone-array data to compare observable signal detection with unique source localization/identity recovery.

discovery_ledger: January Ocean Server and reader question exhibit structural continuity with modern channel/receiver/provenance concepts.
Sea can be modeled more productively as a transceiving physical substrate than as a monolithic server.
42 is useful as a fixed negative-control packet because BA16-style quotienting makes its lost provenance explicit.
formalization_ledger: (i,j,k) -> (i,k) implies irrecoverable j without side information
uniform fiber n gives H(X|Q)=log2(n) and exact-member recovery ceiling 1/n

seal: THE SEA MAY RECEIVE AND SEND A STATE; THE READER MUST PROVE WHAT SOURCE IDENTITY SURVIVED. A RECEIVED ANSWER IS NOT YET ITS QUESTION.
